items.title: Theoretical Limits of Language Model Alignment
items.raw_excerpt: Language model (LM) alignment improves model outputs to reflect human preferences while preserving the capabilities of the base model. The most common alignment approaches are (i) reinforcement learning, which maximizes the expected reward under a KL-divergence constraint, and (ii) best-of-NNN alignment, which selects the highest-reward output among NNN independent samples. Despite their widespread use, the fundamental limits of reward improvement under a KL budget remain poorly understood. items.title: Evaluating the Evaluators: Investigating LLM Judges for Personalized Writing Style Assessment
items.raw_excerpt: This paper was accepted at the Can We Trust AI Evaluation? Workshop at NeurIPS 2026. We evaluate how good large language model (LLM) judges are for personalized writing tasks. This is important when a user’s preferred writing style is known (e.g., “upbeat”) and an LLM judge is used to evaluate whether generated text adheres to this preference. We examine how the writing task, the combination of generator and judge LLM, the evaluation objective, and general commonsense and reasoning ability impact LLM judge performance. items.title: On the Importance of Gating: Memorization vs. In-Context Learning in State Space Models
items.raw_excerpt: State Space Models (SSMs) have emerged as a compelling alternative to Transformers, enabling sequence modeling with constant memory and linear compute. Although SSMs exhibit reasonable performance and favorable computational characteristics, they continue to lag behind Transformers on tasks that require in-context learning and precise retrieval, slowing their adoption for large-scale language modeling. items.raw_excerpt: External memory enables LLM agents to improve from experience by distilling trajectories of past tasks into concise lessons for new tasks. items.raw_excerpt: Early successes on agentic robotics point to a potential paradigm shift toward using coding agents to control robots. Existing robotics benchmarks are built around visuomotor policy learning, leaving it open whether coding agents can reliably control diverse robots under physical-world constraints.
